solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Plover in shot game on roll of grass?

indicators.note: in a down clue, one piece placed on top of the next

parts.note: a kill is the game a hunter has shot

indicators.note: rolling the grass over turns its letters back to front

parts.note: reed is a tall grass

explanation.surface: A hunter's bag of a shot bird lies on a rolled-up strip of turf.
explanation.definitionFit: The killdeer is a noisy North American bird of the plover family, named for its call.

clue.text: One leaving wardens blowing out trick candles

indicators.note: the letter for one is leaving, so it drops out of what remains
blowing out removes the trick's letters from the wardens

parts.note: concierges are doormen or wardens of a building
a con is a trick or swindle
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A party trick where a single guest leaves and the hosts blow out joke candles.
explanation.walkthrough: Take CONCIERGES (wardens), blow out CON (trick) to leave CIERGES, then let I (one) leave.
explanation.definitionFit: Cerges, also spelt cierges, are large wax candles used in church ceremonies.

clue.text: Frank to pop the question at last

indicators.note: the final letter of each of these four words is taken

explanation.surface: Someone called Frank is finally going to propose marriage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Frank' looks like a man's name, but it is the definition, meaning candid.
explanation.definitionFit: Being open is being frank: honest and candid, with nothing hidden.

clue.text: Angular shape of e.g. French nose only intermittently brought up

indicators.note: in a down clue, bringing the letters up reads them bottom to top

parts.note: the abbreviation EG, for example
nez is French for nose

indicators.note: only every other letter of the word is used

explanation.surface: A description of an angular French nose, mentioned only now and then.
explanation.walkthrough: EG + NEZ + OL (alternate letters of 'only') gives EGNEZOL, which 'brought up' reverses.
explanation.definitionFit: A lozenge is a diamond, a rhombus with two acute and two obtuse angles.

clue.text: Veto vacuous church seniors, shifting pressure

indicators.note: the letters are moved around into a new order
an empty church keeps only its outer letters

parts.note: P is the physics symbol for pressure

explanation.surface: Church elders with nothing to say are blocked as the pressure on them shifts.
explanation.walkthrough: CH (church emptied) and SENIORS are rearranged together, then P for pressure ends the word.
explanation.definitionFit: Censorship is official prohibition of material, so it acts as a ban or veto on publication.

clue.text: You and I sold out in reprehensible fashion

indicators.note: out suggests the letters are disordered or put out of place

explanation.surface: An accusation that the two of us betrayed someone shamefully.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters of YOU, I and SOLD are rearranged; 'and' only joins them.
explanation.definitionFit: Odiously means hatefully or detestably, behaving in a way that deserves blame.

clue.text: Rowing over river, stopping a while?

parts.note: O is the cricket scoring abbreviation for an over

indicators.note: the river letter plugs a gap in the following words

parts.note: a while can be an age
R is the map abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: Rowers out on a river halt for a short rest.
explanation.walkthrough: R (river) stops A AGE to make ARAGE, after O.
explanation.definitionFit: Oarage is an old word for rowing, the action of using oars.

clue.text: Quit probing dog from behind: setter has

indicators.note: the setter's letters probe inside the dog
the dog is read from its rear end, backwards

parts.note: a pug is a small breed of dog
the setter says 'I have', contracted to I've

explanation.surface: A dog-handling setter stops examining a dog's rear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'setter' looks like the dog breed alongside 'dog', but it is the crossword setter speaking: I'VE.
explanation.definitionFit: To give up is to stop or abandon an activity, the same as to quit.

clue.text: Embellish when presenting charge returned on deliveries

indicators.note: the reversed word follows after the first piece

parts.note: an over in cricket is a set of six balls delivered

indicators.note: returned means the word is read back to front

parts.note: a ward is a person in one's charge

explanation.surface: Charges for deliveries are padded when presented in an account.
explanation.definitionFit: To overdraw a picture or character is to exaggerate it in the depiction.

clue.text: Polish end of ferrule on bent cane

indicators.note: only the final letter of the word is taken

parts.note: the on side in cricket is also called the leg side

indicators.note: a bent cane has its letters twisted into another order

explanation.surface: Buffing the metal tip on a walking stick that has warped.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Polish' looks like a verb, but it is a noun meaning refinement; the capital letter also hints at the nationality.
explanation.definitionFit: Polish as a noun means refinement and grace of manner, which is elegance.

clue.text: Vehicle number hidden by crap

indicators.note: the number sits concealed inside the crap

parts.note: scat is animal droppings

explanation.surface: A car's number plate covered in dirt.
explanation.definitionFit: A snowcat is a tracked vehicle used for travelling over snow.

clue.text: Gossip's cryptic allusion to REM song?

indicators.note: the answer itself is read as a clue whose result is the band's song

parts.note: the answer, split into a word meaning fresh and a seven-letter remainder, reads as an anagram indicator and fodder making these words

explanation.surface: A gossip hints at the title of a song by the band R.E.M.
explanation.walkthrough: Split the answer NEW SMONGER: 'new' is an anagram signal and SMONGER rearranges to REM SONG.
explanation.definitionFit: A newsmonger is a person who spreads rumours and tittle-tattle, a gossip.

clue.text: Rarely overshadows tramp interrupting awful boaster

indicators.note: the tramp breaks into the middle of the reworked word
an awful boaster is a badly arranged one

parts.note: a bum is a tramp or vagrant

explanation.surface: A vagrant cuts into a braggart's speech, which seldom outshines him.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rarely' belongs to the definition: the word is a rare one. BUM interrupts OBRATES, an anagram of BOASTER.
explanation.definitionFit: Obumbrate is a seldom-used word meaning to cast a shadow over or darken.

clue.text: Reportedly sterilise river

indicators.note: reportedly means the word is as heard spoken

parts.note: to spay is to sterilise a female animal

explanation.surface: News that a river is to be cleaned of germs.
explanation.walkthrough: The Spey is a river in the Scottish Highlands, famous for salmon and whisky.
explanation.definitionFit: The Spey is a river in north-east Scotland, so it is an example of a river.

clue.text: Grumpy old lady keeps centrepiece of pastoral produce for show

indicators.note: the old lady holds the middle letters inside her

parts.note: an old trout is a bad-tempered old woman

indicators.note: only the central pair of letters of the word is used

explanation.surface: A cantankerous farm widow guards the best item in her rural display at the show.
explanation.walkthrough: An old trout is British slang for a grumpy, unpleasant old woman; 'produce' is a verb here, not farm produce.
explanation.definitionFit: To trot out something is to bring it out and display it, often tiresomely.

clue.text: Vehicle boot damaged, horse finally denting back

indicators.note: the boot's letters are knocked out of order
only the final letter of the word is taken
the horse is read backwards

parts.note: a nag is an old horse

explanation.surface: A horse kicks a car's boot in, denting the back.
explanation.walkthrough: TOBO (BOOT damaged) + G (last of 'denting') + GAN (NAG backwards).
explanation.definitionFit: A toboggan is a sledge, a vehicle for sliding down snowy slopes.

clue.text: Old country name banished in calligraphy prior to Reformation?

indicators.note: the remaining letters are re-formed into a new order
the name's letters are expelled from the word

parts.note: to call is to name

explanation.surface: A historical name struck out of a manuscript before the Protestant Reformation.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove CALL (name) from CALLIGRAPHY to leave IGRAPHY, which is re-formed.
explanation.definitionFit: Phrygia was an ancient kingdom in Asia Minor, now part of Turkey.

clue.text: Entire triangle requires reconstruction

indicators.note: the word must be rebuilt with its letters in a new order

explanation.surface: A whole triangle needs to be rebuilt.
explanation.definitionFit: Integral means whole and complete, lacking nothing.

clue.text: Refuse massage twice offered by hotel

parts.note: to rub is to massage
bis is Latin for twice, used in music and addresses
H is hotel in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Turning down a double massage offered by a hotel spa.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Refuse' looks like a verb, but it is the noun meaning waste.
explanation.definitionFit: Refuse as a noun is waste material, which is rubbish.

clue.text: Flamboyance overwhelms essayist and critic

indicators.note: the longer word covers the answer within it

explanation.surface: A literary critic is swamped by showiness.
explanation.definitionFit: Charles Lamb was an English essayist and critic, author of the Essays of Elia.

clue.text: Adult's loose relative

parts.note: A is the film certificate for adult
to loose a knot is to untie it

explanation.surface: A grown-up's relative of easy morals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'loose' looks like an adjective, but it is a verb meaning set free.
explanation.definitionFit: Auntie is a familiar form of aunt, a family member.

clue.text: Reportedly informed on royal plans

indicators.note: reportedly means the words are as heard spoken

parts.note: blew is informed on, as in blew the whistle; a prince is a member of a royal family

explanation.surface: News that someone betrayed a member of the royal family.
explanation.definitionFit: Blueprints are detailed technical drawings, so designs or schemes for a project.

clue.text: Former PM scrapping borders in republic

indicators.note: the first and last letters of the name are thrown away

parts.note: Benjamin Disraeli was a 19th-century British Prime Minister

explanation.surface: An ex-prime minister abolishing the frontiers within a republic.
explanation.definitionFit: Israel is a parliamentary republic in the Middle East.

clue.text: Odd couples expelled in shenanigan mark mystery

indicators.note: taking the phrase in pairs of letters, the first, third, fifth and seventh pairs are thrown out

explanation.surface: Strange pairs are thrown out for leaving a mark of mischief.
explanation.walkthrough: Split SHENANIGANMARK into pairs SH EN AN IG AN MA RK and remove the odd-numbered pairs.
explanation.definitionFit: An enigma is a puzzle or riddle, something baffling.

clue.text: Always in sack by end of large drink

indicators.note: by means beside, so one piece follows the other
the first word goes inside the container

parts.note: a bag is a sack
ever means always

indicators.note: only the final letter of the word is taken

explanation.surface: Someone always keeps a large drink in a bag.
explanation.definitionFit: A beverage is any liquid for drinking other than water.

clue.text: Son enters by way of permit

indicators.note: the son's letter goes inside the following phrase

parts.note: via means by way of
S is the genealogical abbreviation for son

explanation.surface: A son gets into a country by means of an entry document.
explanation.definitionFit: A visa is an official endorsement on a passport permitting entry to a country.

clue.text: In stream, announced Fawlty Towers

indicators.note: Fawlty spoken aloud is faulty, signalling the letters are set wrongly

explanation.surface: Fawlty Towers, the 1970s British sitcom set in a hotel, is broadcast in a stream.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fawlty Towers' reads as the sitcom title, but 'Towers' is the definition and 'Fawlty', said aloud as faulty, is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Minarets are the slender towers of a mosque.

clue.text: Judge apprehended yo-yo

parts.note: to see can mean to judge or consider
saw means perceived or apprehended

explanation.surface: A judge has arrested a toy yo-yo.
explanation.definitionFit: To yo-yo is to fluctuate up and down, as a seesaw does.
